clue.text: Shift operative time of sportsman's appointment

parts.note: a back is a defending player in football, rugby or hockey
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Someone is moving the start time of an athlete's booking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long phrase: to move the date from which something takes effect to an earlier one.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a document effective from an earlier date is exactly to shift the time it starts operating.

clue.text: Corrupt doctor's transport parked in depot

indicators.note: the vehicle is parked within the depot word

parts.note: a base is a depot or headquarters
the TARDIS is the time machine in the British TV series Doctor Who

explanation.surface: A medic's vehicle left at the depot is tampered with.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor is Doctor Who, the British TV time traveller, whose police-box craft is the TARDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bastardise is to debase or spoil something by adding inferior elements.

clue.text: Pocketing raised offer, my character's liable to deteriorate

parts.note: cor is an exclamation like my!

indicators.note: pocketing means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a role is a character played

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a bid is an offer

explanation.surface: Someone takes a bigger bid and admits their character is slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not a possessive here but the British exclamation of surprise; 'raised' in a down clue sends the offer upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something corrodible can be eaten away or worn down, so it may deteriorate.

clue.text: Lived with carnal thoughts upping temperature

indicators.note: upping in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: lewd means having lustful thoughts

explanation.surface: Someone lived with lustful thoughts that raised the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dwelt somewhere is to have resided or lived there.

clue.text: Choir's situation shortly after chorister finds better option

indicators.note: after places the church section following the singer

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano in a choir

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church where the choir sits

explanation.surface: A singer finds a better choice after the choir's position is trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets. The treble chance was a classic British football pools bet on drawn matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble chance is a type of football pools coupon, an option offered to a gambler.

clue.text: Husband in novelist's latest yarn recoils in horror

indicators.note: the husband's letter is placed inside the turned-round tale
recoils means the word for a yarn springs back, read right to left

parts.note: a saga is a long story or yarn

indicators.note: latest means the final letter of the word novelist's

explanation.surface: A husband in a novelist's newest story backs away horrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoils' looks like the verb of the definition but turns SAGA into AGAS; H goes inside to give AGHAS, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is aghast is filled with horror or dismay, a close adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Canal worker, one doomed to carry fallen idol?

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a goner is someone doomed

indicators.note: fallen means toppled over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker on the canal, a doomed figure, must carry a toppled statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen idol' reads as a phrase, but 'fallen' rearranges the word idol before it is carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a gondola along the canals of Venice.

clue.text: Well absolutely empty

indicators.note: to empty a word is to remove its inner letters

explanation.surface: Two words of emphatic agreement read as a statement of emptiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'absolutely' goes, leaving its first two and last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something ably is to do it competently, so well.

clue.text: Old mate featured in Times passage

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside

parts.note: T stands for time, so two of them make times
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A past friend appears in a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper but is a plural of T, time.
explanation.definitionFit: A text is a passage of writing, as when a book extract is set for study.

clue.text: Charmer? More vexed hosts cheer when he's gone

indicators.note: to host is to hold within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: sorer means more annoyed or irritated

indicators.note: the letters H and E are taken away from the word cheer

explanation.surface: A charming man leaves, and an angrier crowd celebrates his departure.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a definition by example: a sorcerer casts charms, so is a charmer of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer works spells or enchantments, so the playful word charmer can describe a wizard.

clue.text: Ten with hip complaint, all coming together

parts.note: in means fashionable, as hip does
flu is an illness, a complaint
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten people with hip trouble all arrive at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' reads as the joint but is the slang sense, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is an arrival of many people or things at once, everything converging together.

clue.text: Tablet walker crunched for afters

indicators.note: crunched means crushed, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A walker with a pill crunched it before dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is British slang for pudding; a Bakewell tart is an English almond and jam pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bakewell tart is a classic English dessert, an example of a pudding.

clue.text: In Rome I love old Latin sparkling wine

parts.note: amo is Latin for I love

indicators.note: sparkling suggests fizz and movement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian love declaration in old Latin, over a fizzy wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkling' seems to describe the wine, but it rearranges OLD LATIN to NTILLADO. The answer is a sherry, not a sparkling wine at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium dry sherry from Spain, which is a fortified wine.

clue.text: Exotic dancer in possession of a vehicle took touring holiday

indicators.note: being in possession of something means holding it within
exotic means unusual, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A striptease artist owns a car of her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic dancer' reads as one phrase but 'Exotic' rearranges DANCER into CARNED, which holds A VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To caravan is to holiday travelling in a towed or motor caravan.

clue.text: Observer's outlook sees very little about the year changing

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: wee is Scottish for very small

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecaster sees little shift over the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the letters of the year to ATHEREY; 'sees' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a weather eye means staying watchful, the alert outlook of a close observer.

clue.text: Harry keeps home functioning

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: to dog someone is to harry or pursue them
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone named Harry keeps his house running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing, as in how is it doing, means operating or performing, so functioning.

clue.text: Noble old lady died, owing about a thousand

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, an old lady

indicators.note: about means surrounding a thousand

parts.note: due means owed
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: An aristocratic old woman died in debt of about a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand duke is a high-ranking nobleman, ruler of a grand duchy.

clue.text: Put small stone inside to make a crackling sound

definitions.note: the clue names the sound; the answer is the verb for producing it

indicators.note: put works with inside to place one piece within another
inside says the stone goes within the verb for making

parts.note: to create is to make
a pit is a small fruit stone

explanation.surface: Instructions: drop a little pebble in to make it rattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'wordplay to make definition'; the answer is a verb meaning to make a crackling sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To crepitate is to crackle or rattle, a word used in medicine for crackling in the lungs.

clue.text: Aunts et al badly treated in Muslim autocracy

indicators.note: something badly treated is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aunts and others are mistreated under a harsh Islamic regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate is a state ruled by a sultan, a Muslim sovereign with absolute power.

clue.text: Respond to order "about turn"

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a turn is a stage act or performance

explanation.surface: A soldier obeys the drill command to face the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about turn' reads as one parade-ground order but is two pieces: RE and ACT, a performer's turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to a stimulus or instruction.

clue.text: Line of French reservists invading lyceum

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: invading means entering, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a lyceum is a school or college
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A row of French reserve soldiers storms a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' suggests soldiers in formation but means a neckline.
explanation.definitionFit: A décolletage is a low neckline on a dress, so the cut or line of the garment.

clue.text: US graduate overlooked climbing plant

indicators.note: overlooked means ignored, so letters are left out

parts.note: the US is America

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: An American graduate fails to notice a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing plant' looks like one phrase, but 'climbing' turns MA to AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heathers, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Strikes up a bit of an argument

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taps means strikes lightly

explanation.surface: Industrial strikes stir up a small row.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief petty quarrel, a minor bout of argument.

clue.text: Large bird with down cut

indicators.note: down in a down clue means moved lower, one place further along

parts.note: a swan is a large waterbird

explanation.surface: A big bird with soft feathers is chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like feathers but tells W, short for with, to drop one place in SWAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn is the past participle of saw, so cut with a saw.

clue.text: Tablet's coating causing harm in mouth

definitions.meaning: a flat inscribed panel fixed to a wall
the bacterial film on teeth that leads to decay

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commemorative wall panel and the film on teeth that causes decay.

clue.text: Sole diversion at island welcomed by coppers

indicators.note: to be welcomed by is to be taken in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: pence are copper coins

explanation.surface: A lone fish's amusement on an island, greeted by policemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish but means solitary; 'coppers' are coins, not police.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a card game played alone, a pastime for a single person.

clue.text: Present set back left-winger after payment of tax

indicators.note: set back means placed in reverse, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
net pay is what remains after tax is paid

explanation.surface: A gift returned to a socialist once the tax bill is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: REDNET is reversed as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to present or offer formally, as in tendering a resignation.

clue.text: Arch over seat accommodating two leaders in trial

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so one piece is held within

parts.note: a saddle is a rider's seat

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word trial

explanation.surface: A bridge over a seat is put to a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something is to span it, extending across from one side to the other.
